text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell sharply over the past week, dropping from $414.65 to $367.19—a nearly 11% decline—with today's small move continuing that downtrend. The steepest drops came on November 18th and 19th, coinciding with escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East: Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery, and Iran-backed drone and projectile strikes were reported against Saudi and Bahraini facilities. Refinery operators depend on stable crude supply and predictable shipping routes, so threats to major production and export hubs directly pressure margins and stock valuations for companies like this.

Reinforcing the negative pressure, the failed climate talks at COP31 (which rejected including fossil fuels in the final deal) signal lengthening headwinds for refining as global policy shifts toward energy transition—a backdrop that weighs on investor confidence in the sector even as U.S. refineries remain busy at 95.7% capacity and crude inventories sit at comfortable levels.
